transcript.text: my tumble dryer is giving off a burning smell?? is it safe to keep using it

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. A burning smell suggests overheating or a mechanical fault that could lead to a fire. You should stop using it immediately and have it checked by a qualified engineer before attempting any further drying cycles. To help diagnose what might be happening once an engineer looks at it, please switch the appliance off and unplug it for safety. Then check if the main fluff filter in the door opening is completely clogged with lint, or if the vent hose at the back of the machine is kinked or blocked.

ok I switched it off at the wall after the second time?? the filter is really full, I haven't cleaned it in a few weeks. the hose behind is squashed and I can see fluff inside the end of it. is that what's causing the smell??

⚠ Stop using this appliance
Yes, that is probably what caused the smell. A filter clogged with lint and a squashed vent hose stop air from flowing properly, which makes the dryer overheat rapidly and can scorch the lint or plastic parts. Because a burning smell suggests a fire risk or internal damage, you must not use the machine again until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. Please clean the filter thoroughly and clear or replace the squashed vent hose to restore airflow, but leave the appliance unplugged for at least an hour to cool down completely before calling someone out.

candidates: Blocked lint filter or vent causing overheating (high)
Drive belt or motor rubbing due to wear (medium)
